cards.title: Neurons are tiny formulas
cards.body:
A **neuron** multiplies each input by a weight, adds them up with a bias, and squashes the result into 0..1 with the **sigmoid** function. Stack neurons in layers and you get a **neural network**.

XOR (1 if exactly one input is 1) can't be solved by one neuron, because no single straight line separates its answers. A hidden layer fixes that.
Every edge label is a weight. Watch them change, and the predictions move towards 0, 1, 1, 0.

**Backpropagation** is the chain rule from calculus applied backwards: the output's error is shared out to each weight in proportion to how much that weight contributed. This app's tests check these updates against a numerical estimate of the gradient, so the maths is verified, not just plausible.

cards.title: From 13 numbers to billions
cards.body: Large AI models use the same ingredients: weighted sums, non-linear functions, a loss, backpropagation and gradient descent. The differences are scale (billions of weights), architecture (how layers connect) and data (enormous training sets).

cards.question: Why can't a single neuron learn XOR?
choices: XOR's answers can't be separated by one straight line
cards.explain: One neuron draws one line (a linear boundary). XOR needs two, which the hidden layer provides.
